name: coopplatformer-2p

webgpu.note: GL vs WebGPU 0.017 percent at frame 400 on the 890M (bound 0.5), every host the same; was 0.5 to 1 percent while WebGPU drew this HDR scene single-sampled: WebGPU now asks for a core device and multisamples it 4x as GL does, resolving the depth for the passes after it (engine: WebGPU core MSAA), and the ambient occlusion no longer darkens the bottom rows on GL alone (engine: the edge normal fix). maxArea catches a surface one backend misses. State exact on every host

note: two bots on the real game flow (title skipped) along the first level: cross-host state and picture.

name: coopplatformer-scenery

webgpu.note: the picture at frame 60 at the start of the meadow, GL vs WebGPU within the same bounds as the 2p gate

note: no floating scenery: every prop that stands on the ground is measured against the ground as drawn. g.scenery_off is the number whose base is more than 3 cm above or below the lowest ground under it or that overhang a ledge or the edge of the backdrop. The control lifts the first meadow tree 0.5 m (COOP_FLOAT_BUG, native): it must differ. Every level is swept by coopplatformer-levels.

name: coopplatformer-fire

webgpu.note: the picture at frame 60 at the start of the first level of the caves, GL vs WebGPU within the same bounds as the scenery gate

note: no floating fire: every flame (one emitter per brazier in the caves and ruins) is checked each frame against the basket of a brazier that the scenery check seated on the floor (within 6 cm). g.flames is [flames, flames not in a seated brazier]. Lava lights and ability crystals carry no flame. The control (COOP_FLOAT_FIRE, native) puts each flame where the old torch flames burned, 1.5 m in front of the playfield at the light: its g.flames must differ.

name: coopplatformer-surfaces
note: no plain surfaces and no seam rails: g.surface is [moving platforms, wooden ledges and cracked blocks built with a real PBR material, the same built with a plain colour, seam strips drawn across rock faces]. The control (COOP_PLAIN_BUG, native) brings back the olive platform and the grey seams: its g.surface must differ. Native only: carts have no environment. g.uvrep: percent of sampled wall corners whose texture phase comes back one 4 m repeat on (100 before the uvs wandered; the same control). Re-pinned 45 to 4: this first level has only 4 built surfaces of that kind (the old level held the whole game); the same check runs on the level that is loaded.

name: coopplatformer-pit-camera
note: the camera never looks under the world: two bots start in the first level's spike pit (x 80 to 86, floor at y 1, the deepest place in it) and fight their way out. g.underview is [frames drawn, frames whose view reached below the world floor row]; the camera target is held so the bottom edge of the view stays above y 0 (a player at the pit floor stays inside the bottom of the frame). The control (COOP_PIT_CAM_BUG, native) lets the camera follow down: its g.underview must differ. Native only: carts have no environment.

name: coopplatformer-rescue-tags
note: the RESCUE tags of players carried in bubbles never run into each other: three of four players are held in bubbles (COOP_TEST_BUBBLES, native). g.tags is [frames with two or more tags, frames where a tag starts before the word of the tag beside it ends (measured with the font)]. The control (COOP_HUD_BUG, native) brings back the old fixed 90 px step: its g.tags must differ. Native only: carts have no environment. g.marker_over counts markers drawn over the player panels: one bubble is held off the top of the view; the same control brings back the old clamp.

name: coopplatformer-blink
note: invulnerable after a respawn, a player pulses with a soft glow and is never hidden: two bots start invulnerable and g.vanish counts frames in which every player on the field was hidden (only markers left on screen). The control (COOP_BLINK_BUG, native) brings back the old on/off blink with a 2-tick phase offset: its g.vanish must differ. Native only: carts have no environment.

name: coopplatformer-boss

webgpu.note: GL vs WebGPU 0.004 percent on the last frame on the 890M (bound 0.5), every host the same; was 0.5 to 1 percent while WebGPU drew this HDR scene single-sampled: WebGPU now asks for a core device and multisamples it 4x as GL does, resolving the depth for the passes after it (engine: WebGPU core MSAA), and the ambient occlusion no longer darkens the bottom rows on GL alone (engine: the edge normal fix). maxArea catches a surface one backend misses. State exact on every host

note: two bots from the arena door of the first boss with every ability: boss fight, hit-stops and the win, cross-host state. g.bossgate is [its kind + 1, frames it was alive in view, hits it took, frames drawn since it died]; the control (COOP_LEVEL, native) starts a level with no boss in it: its g.bossgate must differ. The frames end on the results card, before the next level: g.level says so. No shake: the drawn camera stays smooth through the whole fight, the boss leaps, hits and its death included (g.camgate: frames in motion, none over the bounds), and g.camoffset holds the drawn camera against the follow camera on the frames within half a second of each impact (none off by over 0.1 mm). The impacts are felt in the pads: rumble.sent counts the requests to each player, cw.rumble is the engine's last (the boss going down, pad 1).

name: coopplatformer-camera-1p

webgpu.note: GL vs WebGPU 0.051 percent on the last frame on the 890M (bound 0.5), every host the same; was 0.5 to 1 percent while WebGPU drew this HDR scene single-sampled: WebGPU now asks for a core device and multisamples it 4x as GL does, resolving the depth for the passes after it (engine: WebGPU core MSAA), and the ambient occlusion no longer darkens the bottom rows on GL alone (engine: the edge normal fix). maxArea catches a surface one backend misses. note: camera stability, the way a person plays: one pad through title, join and start, then stand, walk, stop, jump and stand while the drawn camera is measured every frame (g.camgate: frames at rest, at-rest frames that moved over 1 mm, frames in motion, frames in motion with a jump over 0.6 m or a jerk over 8 cm). At rest it must not move at all (but for that glide); in motion it must stay smooth. The control puts a 1 cm sway on the drawn camera (COOP_CAM_BUG, native): its g.camgate must differ.

note: camera stability, the way a person plays: four pads through title, join and start (only pad 1 plays after that, so five seconds in the three others are seats nobody plays and the view glides off them onto player 1 over two seconds: the 13 at-rest frames that move are that glide, smooth, no jump or jerk), then stand, walk, stop, jump and stand while the drawn camera is measured every frame (g.camgate: frames at rest, at-rest frames that moved over 1 mm, frames in motion, frames in motion with a jump over 0.6 m or a jerk over 8 cm). At rest it must not move at all; in motion it must stay smooth. The control puts a 1 cm sway on the drawn camera (COOP_CAM_BUG, native): its g.camgate must differ.

name: coopplatformer-coins

webgpu.note: the picture at frame 60 at the start of the meadow, GL vs WebGPU within the same bounds as the scenery gate

note: every coin stands up: g.coinface is [coins, coins whose disc axis is not level]. Each coin spins about its upright axis through its node and its disc is stood up by its mesh; a coin whose axis has any part along world up lies flat like a plate, edge on to the camera for ever. The control (COOP_COIN_FLAT_BUG, native) leaves the coins flat as they were: its g.coinface must differ.

name: coopplatformer-reach
note: from real movement, every coin, pedestal, flag, cracked wall and room of every level can be reached and no coin sits in rock (reach.c). Control: the levels as they were (COOP_REACH_OLD) must fail.

name: coopplatformer-jump-standing

webgpu.note: the same frame on both backends

note: the standing jump, held input on the real game, from a standstill with the stick and jump pressed together. g.jump is [distance, rise, speed at takeoff]: the short one the running gate is measured against. The control is the running gate's input: its g.jump must differ.

name: coopplatformer-jump-running

webgpu.note: the same frame on both backends

note: West (X) held: speed builds to its top in a second and the jump from it goes about twice as far and a metre and a quarter higher than the standing one. The control is the same input with West let go (a walk and a jump): its g.jump must differ.

name: coopplatformer-music-file
note: every track decodes in a second, independent player, runs its form with no silence or clipping, and its restart is not a click. Control: a track with no notes.

name: coopplatformer-levels
note: every level finished by bots with 1, 2 and 4 players, and every level grounded. Controls: bots that never hold Run do not finish the first level; a lifted tree shows.

name: coopplatformer-touch

webgpu.note: the same frame on both backends

note: touch still plays it: the stick, a held RUN button and the jump button give the same running jump as the pad. The control lets go of RUN: its g.jump must differ. Speed 9.86 not 11.5: this stick is pushed to about 0.86 of its throw, and a run scales with the stick.

name: coopplatformer-gore

webgpu.note: the picture with particles in the air: the same frame on both backends

note: two bots against the hedge trimmer on the real cart: g.gore is [deaths seen, played as a big gag, stains on the level]. The control (COOP_NO_GORE, native) plays none: its g.gore must differ. The picture is compared across GL and WebGPU with blood in the air.

name: coopplatformer-pit-fall

webgpu.note: the same frame on both backends

note: walking off the first gap with a real pad: the camera stays above the lip and watches the body drop out of the picture. g.pitview is [frames someone was below the lip of a pit, of them frames the camera went below it]. The control (COOP_PIT_CAM_BUG, native) lets the camera follow down: it must differ.

name: coopplatformer-near-layer

webgpu.note: the same frame on both backends

note: the near layer between the camera and the play never stands in front of a player: g.nearcover is [players drawn, of them with the layer above their feet along the line of sight]. The control (COOP_NEAR_BUG, native) stands it 7 m higher: it must differ.

name: coopplatformer-throw

webgpu.note: the same frame on both backends

note: two real pads: the first picks up the second with the left shoulder and throws. g.throws counts it. The control does not press the button: its state must differ.

name: coopplatformer-signs

webgpu.note: the same frame on both backends

note: a sign can always be read and never hides a player, and it does not chase them round the screen: four bots run the first level past its signs. Its words are a caption with a place of their own, top centre, or the bottom when a player comes up there. g.signgate is [frames a sign was up, of them over a player's body, of them drawn thin over a player]; g.signmove is [times it changed place, frames it was faded or held back for that, a player marker under its place counting too]. The control (COOP_SIGN_BUG, native) leaves it over the board and thins it when a player is near, as it was: its g.signgate must differ.

name: coopplatformer-words
note: words never sit on words or on a marker, four players at 200% text: four bots run the first level past its signs. g.wordsgate is [frames with words up, of them with the sign's caption on a player marker, of them with two boxes of words (the caption, a boss's words, what players say) overlapping]. The control (COOP_WORDS_BUG, native) lets the caption ignore the markers and the words ignore each other: its g.wordsgate must differ.

name: coopplatformer-words-boss
note: the boss fight with four players at 200% text: the boss's words and what the players say never stack (g.wordsgate as in coopplatformer-words). The control (COOP_WORDS_BUG) stacks them: its g.wordsgate must differ.

name: coopplatformer-results-card

webgpu.note: the card over the arena, the same frame on both backends

note: the results card can be read: g.cardgate is [frames it was up, of them with the player portraits on the line above them, levels of the whole game whose closing line takes two rows and so runs into that line]. That the card is solid is measured in the picture by coopplatformer-arena. The control (COOP_CARD_BUG, native) puts the portraits and the wrap back as they were: its g.cardgate must differ.

name: coopplatformer-shadows
note: no hero or enemy throws a sun shadow (on the hills behind the play they were dark figures of their own, read as enemies); each stands on a soft contact blob instead. g.blobs is [characters drawn this frame, of them with a blob, blobs under a player standing on a floor that are not at the floor (none: nothing floats)]. g.charshadow counts heroes that throw a sun shadow. The control (COOP_SHADOW_OLD, native) brings the sun shadows back and drops the blobs: its g.charshadow must differ.

name: coopplatformer-rim
note: the heroes carry a rim of their own colour, strong in the caves and the crater, so the four read against navy and red (the contrast is measured in frames in the fun-graphics notes). g.rim counts materials with a rim. The control (COOP_RIM_OFF, native) leaves the rims off: its g.rim must differ.

name: coopplatformer-hint

webgpu.note: the same frame on both backends

note: the hint line retires once each half has been done: a running jump that went far (over 7.5 m at more than 80 percent of the top speed) and a return to the last flag (held Retry; or the third level reached). Both halves stay in the pause menu. g.hint is [frames the line was drawn, the halves still up: bit 0 the running jump, bit 1 the flag]. The input runs, jumps far and holds Retry. The control walks instead of running (a walking jump of about 6 m) and holds Retry: the running half stays, so its g.hint must differ.

name: coopplatformer-tally
note: the results card counts each player: coins, stomps, friends thrown and falls in a column under each portrait, and an awards line for whoever got the most of something (a clear winner only). g.tally is [columns drawn, frames the awards line was up]; g.cardgate as in coopplatformer-results-card. The control (COOP_TALLY_OFF, native) leaves the tally off: its g.tally must differ.

name: coopplatformer-save
note: a save from version 4 (before the big coins) loads with its settings and progress: the stored block tests/coopplatformer-save-v4.dat keeps level, unlocked levels, coins, abilities, totals, hats, screen shake and music volume, and the big coins start empty. Control: with the migration off the shell starts over and the check must fail.

name: coopplatformer-arena
note: all five boss arenas with the fight pushed against the end wall: the wall takes no more than 12 percent of the view, no arm goes into it, no words land on a marker or a player, and the results card is solid in the picture on GL and WebGPU. Each has a control that must fail in every arena: the old camera, the old boss width, the old labels, the old card.

name: coopplatformer-controls
note: each control above run for its gate's own frames: the field the gate is about (its controlField) must differ from the value it expects. Control: no control at all must leave the field as expected, which this would report.

name: coopplatformer-quality
note: a program for everything drawn at every quality on both backends, through a spread warm-up as a player gets it: along the whole world, two and four players, the map, bubbles, each of the five bosses fought to its end (g.bossgate), from the title by real input. A scene not reached fails. Controls: a state the scene draws out of the table must be reported and skip draws, on a level and on a boss; a level with no boss must not count as a boss fight
